title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with Online Table Repacking and Query Planning Controls
gist: PostgreSQL 19 ships online table repacking (REPACK CONCURRENTLY), query-plan advice extensions (pg_plan_advice, pg_stash_advice), read-your-writes via WAIT FOR LSN, logical replication of sequences, and security/default changes (TLS SNI, MD5 warnings, JIT off by default, LZ4 TOAST compression). The release targets lower administrative overhead and better performance, though some users advise waiting for 19.1 on critical systems.

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19 adds REPACK, which reclaims unused table space and can reorder data to match an index, and its CONCURRENTLY option runs without blocking reads or writes, positioning it as a replacement for common uses of VACUUM FULL and CLUSTER.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Removes a long-standing downtime pain in Postgres operations and erodes the value of third-party online-repack tooling.
insights.locator: One of the main additions is REPACK

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19 introduces the pg_plan_advice and pg_stash_advice extensions, letting administrators influence query plan selection and apply stored advice to queries by identifier without changing application code.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Native plan-hint control narrows a feature gap versus commercial databases like Oracle and SQL Server, helping migrations to Postgres.

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19 adds parallel index vacuuming, autovacuum prioritization changes and new monitoring views, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE now reports asynchronous I/O activity and WAL generated for full-page images.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Better observability of I/O and WAL reduces operational overhead for large Postgres fleets.
insights.locator: Other maintenance improvements include parallel index vacuuming

insights.claim: PostgreSQL reports that changes to foreign key checks made bulk inserts nearly twice as fast in testing in version 19.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Material ingest speedups strengthen Postgres for write-heavy workloads.
insights.quote: bulk inserts nearly twice as fast in testing
insights.locator: PostgreSQL also reports that changes to foreign key checks

insights.claim: The PostgreSQL 19 planner adds more efficient anti-joins for eligible NOT IN clauses and eager aggregation before joins.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Analytical query improvements expand Postgres' reach into reporting workloads.

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19 disables JIT compilation by default because its cost estimates proved unreliable, and makes LZ4 the default TOAST compression method when supported by the build.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Default changes can shift performance on upgrade; operators should benchmark JIT-dependent workloads.
insights.locator: JIT compilation is now disabled by default

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19 logical replication now supports sequence values, and the server automatically raises the effective WAL level to logical when the first logical replication slot is created.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Simplifies zero-downtime major-version upgrades and CDC pipelines built on Postgres.
insights.locator: Logical replication now supports sequence values

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19's new WAIT FOR LSN command lets applications wait until a standby has replayed a given WAL position before querying, providing read-your-writes consistency on replicas.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Makes read-replica scaling safer for consistency-sensitive apps, reducing need for custom routing middleware.
insights.locator: The new WAIT FOR LSN command

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19 adds INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO SELECT for get-or-create operations, JSON output from COPY, more SQL/JSON string methods, and IGNORE NULLS for window functions.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Continued developer-ergonomics gains reinforce Postgres as the default application database.
insights.locator: Developers also get INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO SELECT

insights.claim: PostgreSQL 19 adds server-side TLS Server Name Indication so one server can present different certificates by client hostname, and warns after successful MD5 password authentication ahead of MD5's planned removal in favor of SCRAM.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Operators still on MD5 auth face a forced migration; SNI eases multi-tenant hosting.
insights.locator: Security and compatibility changes include server-side TLS

insights.claim: Hacker News users debated whether production users should wait for PostgreSQL 19.1, with one recommending waiting for the first minor release on critical production systems.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Expect enterprise adoption of 19 to lag until the first minor release.
insights.quote: for critical production systems, it's still good to wait for the .1 release
insights.locator: The release has also prompted discussion on Hacker News
